Teaching map · K–5, 6th, 7th, 8th

Science Lessons, K–5 to 8th Grade

Open any file in a web browser (internet needed for fonts only). All 32 interactive lessons, sorted into K–5, sixth, seventh and eighth grade folders, are listed in a recommended teaching order, with what each builds on. Tap a unit to open it. Every lesson also links to related pages at the bottom and mentions earlier ideas at the top ("you may already have learned").

How to use this map

Start with the K–5 How Science Works unit (Unit 0: origins of science, the scientific method, hypotheses, fair tests). Then follow the numbered order, now split into the k-5/, 6th/, 7th/ and 8th/ folders. Side trips (Units 10 to 13) are extra sixth-grade units that fit best after the unit named in their opening note; you can skip them and come back. Seventh and eighth grade continue in order. Sixth grade starts at Unit 1 once the K–5 method unit is done. Each unit is about five 30-minute sessions. Every lesson ends with a short browser game that practices its core idea; no install or login is needed.

Science Arcade

Six quick browser games (gravity, light, circuits, levers, states of matter, football physics) for warm-ups and rainy days: open the Science Arcade. Every lesson above also has its own game built in at the end.

The method unit that starts the whole sequence. It is being fleshed out; more K–5 material will land here.

Not covered yet

Units that are still missing from the plan: electric circuits (current, voltage, series and parallel), Earth's climate and climate change (beyond Unit 13), human body health topics (nutrition, disease and the immune system), chemistry of acids and bases, simple machines and work, and data analysis and statistics as its own mini-unit. High school is out of scope.

Standards mappings (NGSS performance expectations) in each lesson footer are approximate and should be checked against the OpenSciEd alignment pages and the Michigan Science Standards. Source programs: OpenSciEd and Michigan Virtual. This map is a plan, not an official Ann Arbor Public Schools sequence.
